title: Create a PRD proposal for preserving chat scroll position during
specification:
Create a PRD proposal for preserving chat scroll position during polling updates.

Problem: The chat window jumps back to the bottom whenever interval updates refresh the chat, interrupting users who are reading earlier messages.

Goal: Keep the user's chat scroll position stable during background refreshes, while still scrolling to the latest message when appropriate.

Requirements:
1. Detect whether the user is near the bottom before refreshed messages render.
2. Only auto-scroll when the user is near the bottom, sends a message, or clicks a jump-to-latest action.
3. Preserve visible scroll position when the user has scrolled up and polling updates arrive.
4. Show a lightweight new messages / jump to latest affordance when new content arrives while scrolled up.
5. Apply this to the repo chat window without changing unrelated PRD/task queue scrolling unless shared chat logic requires it.

Acceptance criteria:
- Background polling no longer forces the chat viewport to the bottom while the user is reading older messages.
- Sending a message still scrolls to the latest message/response.
- If the user is already near the bottom, incoming updates keep the latest content visible.
- A scrolled-up user can return to the latest message with one clear action.
- Existing chat send and chat-to-PRD proposal flows continue working.
